newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokai Aluminum unit to boost security tag output.
newsitem.headline: Tokai Aluminum unit to boost security tag output.

text.p: Tokai Electronics Co Ltd, a unit of Tokai Aluminum Foil Co Ltd, said on Thursday it plans to drastically increase its output of security tags designed to prevent shop-lifting.
It plans to make 150 million of the tags a month, compared with the current output of 50 million tags a month, Tokai Electronics said.
Tokai Electronics is 50 percent owned by Tokai Aluminum.
Shops use the tags to protect goods against shop-lifters.

More than 90 percent of the tags, which are in the form of disposable seals, are for export but demand in Japan for protection against shop-lifters is also increasing, a Tokai Electronics official said.
"More than 90 percent are for exports to the United States and Europe," he said.
"But domestic demand is increasing as well," he added.

Japanese shops used to be afraid of losing customers if they introduced anti-shoplifting measures such as monitoring, but that attitude is changing as these days many youngsters steal from stores without any sense of guilt, he said.
